title: A Place That Knows Nobody
summary: At Rowan Hold, no one mistakes Kael for anybody. The community's attention is on Nessa Rowan, who has been chosen to inherit a family obligation she does not want and intends to leave instead.

panelPlan.text: Rowan Hold is a close agricultural settlement gathered around shade trees and low stone houses. An exposed black Sunforge arc crosses the common yard and is used as ordinary seating.
Kael, Eva and Jessa enter expecting another recognition. People glance at them, then go back to a loud family argument around Nessa and her mother Ada.
Eva waits for somebody to call Kael a name. Nobody does. Jessa notices Nessa's packed bag instead.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: They're looking. They just don't care.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I could get used to this.

dialogueInline.speaker: Ada Rowan
dialogueInline.text: You said that before they chose you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Nessa
dialogueInline.text: They chose me because they thought I'd stop saying it.

directionInline.text: This issue is a deliberate negative case for the Kael pattern. The local story must be allowed to matter more than the absence of mystery.

title: Chosen to Stay
summary: Nessa explains that the family selected her to maintain the household records and mediate kin disputes after her aunt's death. It is an honor that would also keep her at Rowan Hold indefinitely. Jessa understands the trap without treating the community as cruel.

panelPlan.text: Nessa shows Eva and Jessa the family room where births, debts, marriages and old agreements are kept in hand-written ledgers.
Ada explains that somebody trustworthy has to remember what everyone promised when tempers were cooler.
Nessa says she loves these people and still does not want the life they have decided proves she loves them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Ada Rowan
dialogueInline.text: Mira trusted her with every name we have.

dialogueInline.speaker: Nessa
dialogueInline.text: She trusted me to help. She did not appoint me from the grave.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Could you do it for a year?

dialogueInline.speaker: Nessa
dialogueInline.text: My uncle said a year. My mother said until they train someone. Nobody has named the someone.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: How long did Mira do it?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: That's what I'd be worried about.

dialogueInline.speaker: Ada Rowan
dialogueInline.text: And what would you have us do? Forget everything?

dialogueInline.speaker: Nessa
dialogueInline.text: No. Figure it out without deciding I already volunteered.

directionInline.text: Do not make Ada a villain. The family genuinely needs continuity and genuinely loves Nessa; the conflict is about converting affection and competence into obligation.

title: What Jessa Notices
summary: While Kael helps with an ordinary meal and nobody projects a false identity onto him, Eva realizes Jessa is more invested in Nessa's decision than she is admitting.

panelPlan.text: Kael sits with two children shelling beans badly but patiently. Nobody asks who he used to be.
Across the yard, Jessa checks Nessa's packed bag for weight and quietly removes things that will be useless on the road.
Eva joins her and starts asking about Nessa, then notices she is really asking about Jessa.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Did somebody do that for you?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: No. That's how I learned about the socks.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: It was enough to get me on the road.

directionInline.text: This is one of the first Eva/Jessa conversations where Kael is not actually the subject. Jessa gives something real without being forced into a full biography.

title: A Vote Against Her
summary: The Rowan family tries to resolve the dispute by voting on whether Nessa should accept the role. Kael points out, gently, that a vote about somebody else's life cannot create consent.

panelPlan.text: Family members gather in the common yard and begin an earnest vote, each explaining why Nessa is needed.
Nessa stands outside the circle that is deciding her future. Jessa is visibly irritated but lets Nessa speak first.
Kael, asked whether travelers have a custom for this, says the obvious thing the family has managed not to say.

dialogueInline.speaker: Nessa
dialogueInline.text: You're taking a vote on whether I get to leave.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Does the person carrying it get a vote?

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Gladly. I only asked because Nessa wasn't inside your circle.

dialogueInline.speaker: Nessa
dialogueInline.text: I love you. I'm leaving anyway.

directionInline.text: Kael does not solve Rowan governance. His outside perspective is useful only because the community is caught inside its own assumptions.

title: The Empty Chair
summary: Once Nessa's departure is treated as real, the family begins asking a different question: how to distribute the work among people who are actually willing. Jessa helps Nessa prepare without romanticizing the road.

panelPlan.text: The ledger room now has several relatives arguing over which pieces of the work each can realistically take.
Nessa and Ada pack together in uneasy silence before Ada finally adds a family recipe book to Nessa's bag.
Eva expects Jessa to congratulate Nessa. Jessa instead warns her about loneliness, money and the fact that leaving does not make every decision correct.

dialogueInline.speaker: Nessa
dialogueInline.text: You make the road sound miserable.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You should put that on a recruiting poster.

dialogueInline.speaker: Nessa
dialogueInline.text: Why did you stay out there?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: Because when I woke up wanting to leave, I could.

directionInline.text: Jessa's road instinct gains human texture without locking a hidden conspiracy or tragic origin. Eva learns to accept a partial answer.

title: Nothing Happened to Kael
summary: The trio leaves Rowan Hold after two uneventful days. Eva is almost offended that Kael was simply Kael the entire time; Jessa recognizes the value of that fact.

panelPlan.text: Nessa walks out on a different road with another small caravan while her family watches without pretending to be happy about it.
Kael says goodbye to people who know him only as Kael. A child returns the knife he loaned for supper prep.
On the road, Eva looks back at the obvious Sunforge arc in the common yard and finally admits the lack of an event is evidence too.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: There was a Sunforge in the yard.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: There was a goat on it most of yesterday.

directionInline.text: End by treating absence as meaningful without pretending one quiet stop disproves the larger pattern.
